maria: Heads up — CloudPSP (reseller) just pinged us about a payout shortfall for Feb GCP Marketplace. They say the invoice shows committed-tier pricing but the partner payout CSV uses list rates. Can someone take a quick look? :eyes:
ashok: Can you paste the invoice line + the payout CSV row they attached?
maria: Invoice PDF (copied line):
```
Invoice: INV-2026-02-3021
SKU: redwood_dedicated_m0
Quantity: 120
Gross unit price: $0.80
Committed discount: 25% -> Net unit price: $0.60
Line net: $72.00
```
Payout CSV row they sent:
```
gcp_sku,units,unit_price,adjustment
redwood_dedicated_m0,120,0.80,0.00
```
maria: They flagged that their payout file (what GCP paid the reseller) shows 0.80, not 0.60. So partner received less credit than expected.
james: billing-bot exports usually include a pricing mapping step. @billing-bot can you confirm which price profile was used for that merchant_id on 2026-02-28? :thinking_face:
billing-bot: export job completed for merchant=cloudpsp on 2026-02-28. Pricing profile used: PROFILE_PUBLIC_V1.
ashok: that's the problem — PROFILE_PUBLIC_V1 is the list-rate profile. The committed-tier should be PROFILE_COMMITTED_25. How did public profile get selected for that merchant?
sophie: I opened a partner support case with GCP partner support (ticket #GP-88421). They responded that marketplace metering used the SKU mapping that matched our legacy SKU alias (redwood_dedicated_m0 -> redwood_m0_legacy) which hasn't been associated with the committed profile. They requested we update the mapping in Cloud Console.
james: Did we recently change any channel-level mappings or migrate SKUs for the Dedicated offering? I remember a SKU rename during the Jan rollout.
maria: We did rename redwood_dedicated_m0 -> redwood_m0_2026-rename on Jan 18. The marketplace connector has a fallback that maps legacy aliases, but looks like the committed profile was attached to the new SKU only.
ashok: Action: either attach the committed pricing profile to the legacy alias in GCP console, or apply a one-off reconciliation credit to the partner for Feb. Which path is faster?
sophie: GCP said changes to mapping take 24-48h and will not retroactively change payouts for processed payouts. So we need a manual adjustment for Feb.
james: I'll pull the payout reconciliation report and compute the shortfall. Give me 30m.
maria: Thanks. Also partner asked for a signed confirmation they will receive a credit before they escalate. Budget owner, can AP approve a ~$120 credit to CloudPSP pending reconciliation?
ashok: Please attach the calculated amount once James posts it. AP needs invoice # and proof of mapping bug.
james: Quick calc from raw: expected net = 120 * 0.60 = 72.00; actual net = 120 * 0.80 = 96.00 -> Wait that shows partner got more, not less. Hmm double-checking math.
maria: Sorry typo — our invoice unit price was $0.60 net (we bill end-customer), but reseller payout should reflect our committed discount in the payout table. Partner claims they were underpaid by $24 because their expected payout included an additional reseller margin pass-through. Their spreadsheet shows expected payout line = $96 but actual payout = $72 (they expected to receive $96 after their margin).
james: Ok confusing. Need the partner's expected formula. Can they share the CSV that includes their margin column?
maria: Attached their export snippet:
```
sku,units,partner_margin_pct,expected_payout
redwood_dedicated_m0,120,10,96.0
```
They expected GCP to apply our committed net (0.60) and then add their 10% margin. GCP applied list-price 0.80 and did not add margin (their reconciliation shows 0.80*120 = 96 but payout after platform fee = 72).
sophie: TL;DR: mismatch of SKU->profile mapping + different payout pipeline assumptions. We'll owe them a reconciliation credit to match their expected settlement.
ashok: Estimated correction requested by partner: $24 (they reported), plus potential fees. Finance: we can do a one-time credit memo to the reseller account and reflect as marketplace adjustment. Need AP approval.
maria: I'll draft the credit memo. @james please paste the final computed delta and the billing-bot export link for audit.
james: Delta computed per partner spreadsheet = $24. Full reconciliation file saved at: s3://redwood-billing/gcp/reconciliations/2026-02/cloudpsp-delta-1799504444.csv
billing-bot: reconciliation export available: https://internal.redwood/billing/exports/1799504444 (md5:5d41402abc4b2a76)
ashok: Approver list: @ashok (RevOps), @maria (Finance), @kelly (AP). Maria can you route to Kelly?
maria: Yep routing to Kelly now. kelly, need approval to issue credit memo CM-2026-02-004 for $24 to CloudPSP to correct GCP marketplace payout mismatch. Supporting docs: invoice INV-2026-02-3021, reconciliation file, partner email, GCP ticket GP-88421.
maria: kelly? :wave: (pings in #people-ops channel as well)
ashok: Also note we should prevent recurrence: assign engineering ops to update marketplace mapping and add unit test to exporter to prefer committed profile when merchant has commit flag. @james can you take a follow-up?
james: Yep I'll own the fix. Will submit a PR to marketplace-connector and add an integration test that simulates a legacy alias. ETA EOD tomorrow.
sophie: I'll keep partner informed. I told them we'll issue credit within 5 business days once approved and share the ticket link.
maria: Thanks all. Leaving thread open until CM is posted. :thumbsup:
